+def _group_clause(tlist, cls):
+    """Group a clause without crossing its container's boundaries."""
+    tidx, token = tlist.token_next_by(m=cls.M_OPEN)
+    while token:
+        # Parenthesis (and other delimited groups) exclude their delimiters
+        # from the groupable range. Statements keep their trailing semicolon.
+        end_idx = tlist.token_index(tlist._groupable_tokens[-1]) + 1
+        for eidx in range(tidx + 1, end_idx):
+            next_ = tlist.tokens[eidx]
+            if next_.match(*cls.M_CLOSE):
+                end_idx = eidx
+                break
+            if isinstance(tlist, (sql.Begin, sql.Parenthesis)):
+                # Only direct punctuation tokens terminate a clause: strings
+                # and nested groups may contain semicolons of their own.
+                if next_.match(T.Punctuation, ';'):
+                    end_idx = eidx
+                    break
+            if isinstance(tlist, sql.Begin) and next_.match(*sql.Begin.M_CLOSE):
+                end_idx = eidx
+                break
+        tlist.group_tokens(cls, tidx, end_idx, include_end=False)
+        tidx, token = tlist.token_next_by(m=cls.M_OPEN, idx=tidx)
+

+import pytest
+import sqlparse
+from sqlparse import sql, tokens as T
+
+
+def checked_parse(text):
+    statements = sqlparse.parse(text)
+    assert len(statements) == 1
+    statement = statements[0]
+    assert str(statement) == text
+    def check_parents(group):
+        for token in group.tokens:
+            assert token.parent is group
+            if token.is_group:
+                check_parents(token)
+    check_parents(statement)
+    return statement
+
+
+def children(group, cls):
+    return [token for token in group.tokens if isinstance(token, cls)]
+
+
+def test_sibling_clauses_in_begin():
+    text = ('BEGIN SELECT x FROM t WHERE x > 0 QUALIFY n = 1; '
+            'SELECT y FROM u QUALIFY m = 2; END;')
+    statement = checked_parse(text)
+    block, = children(statement, sql.Begin)
+    where, = children(block, sql.Where)
+    assert str(where) == 'WHERE x > 0 '
+    assert [str(c) for c in children(block, sql.Qualify)] == [
+        'QUALIFY n = 1', 'QUALIFY m = 2']
+    assert sum(t.match(T.Punctuation, ';') for t in block.tokens) == 2
+    assert block.tokens[-1].match(T.Keyword, 'END')
+    assert not children(where, sql.Qualify)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('clause', ['WHERE', 'QUALIFY'])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('terminator', [';', ''])
+def test_begin_tail_preserves_end(clause, terminator):
+    statement = checked_parse(
+        f'BEGIN SELECT x FROM t {clause} x = 1 {terminator} END;')
+    block, = children(statement, sql.Begin)
+    cls = sql.Where if clause == 'WHERE' else sql.Qualify
+    grouped, = children(block, cls)
+    assert str(grouped) == f'{clause} x = 1 ' + (
+        '' if terminator else ' ')
+    assert block.tokens[-1].match(T.Keyword, 'END')
+    assert sum(t.match(T.Punctuation, ';') for t in block.tokens
+               ) == bool(terminator)
+
+
+def test_nested_parenthesis_statement_boundaries():
+    text = ("SELECT ((SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = ';' QUALIFY n = ';'; "
+            "SELECT y FROM u WHERE y = 2 QUALIFY m = 2;))")
+    statement = checked_parse(text)

spec.question:
Make WHERE and QUALIFY clauses individually navigable when a parsed BEGIN/END block contains multiple SELECT statements. Expose a public `sqlparse.sql.Qualify` TokenList subclass and support QUALIFY grouping at statement level and within nested groups; WHERE must end before a following QUALIFY.

For `BEGIN SELECT x FROM t WHERE x > 0 QUALIFY n = 1; SELECT y FROM u QUALIFY m = 2; END;`, the Begin must have one direct Where child and two separate direct Qualify children. Each internal semicolon must remain outside the clause it terminates, and the closing END must remain a direct child of Begin. A final clause must also leave END outside its range when there is no semicolon before END.

Apply the same semicolon boundary rule to WHERE and QUALIFY inside Parenthesis groups, including nested parentheses. Only a punctuation semicolon at the clause's container level terminates it: semicolons inside strings or nested groups must not do so. Enclosing parenthesis delimiters must remain outside the clauses.

QUALIFY otherwise ends before ORDER BY, LIMIT, UNION, UNION ALL, EXCEPT, or INTERSECT, or at the end of the current container's content. Preserve WHERE's existing keyword boundaries, adding QUALIFY as a boundary. Whitespace preceding a boundary stays in the clause. At ordinary statement level, retain the existing end-of-range convention, including a trailing semicolon when no terminating keyword intervenes. Preserve SQL round-tripping, statement-type detection, and parent relationships.

Return a unified diff against production files only; leave tests unchanged.
